answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by gating entry into a shared lagoon: every identity must lock 10 tokens in a registry contract that computes a unique key from the agent's signing key and slashes it on double-voting. Each extra plume of fake identities costs the attacker 10 fresh tokens plus slashing risk, so 1,000 sybils burn 10,000 tokens. The protocol runs like a sonnet — fixed stanzas of stake, verify, slash — making mass forgery economically irrational.
